When turned on, the app automatically scans incoming text messages in the background to deliver near-instant alerts. You will receive an immediate push notification telling you whether the message is safe or a threat.\n\nThis active protection keeps you informed instantly, stopping phishing attempts before you even open the message!
Also scan messages from WhatsApp, Telegram, and other messaging apps

When enabled, senders whose messages are flagged as high-risk phishing attempts will be automatically added to your blacklist. Future messages from these senders will be silently blocked.\n\nThis helps you stay protected without needing to manually review and block each flagged contact.

Deep Analysis sends your incoming messages to a secure server for enhanced AI-powered scanning using our CNN-Bi-GRU model. This provides a more thorough evaluation than local scanning alone.\n\nRequires an active internet connection. No personally identifiable information is stored on our servers.

When a message contains a URL, it will be verified against known threat databases and security providers to determine if the link leads to a phishing or malicious site.\n\nRequires an active internet connection. Only the URL is checked — your message content is not transmitted.

Browse our FAQ for quick answers to common questions, or contact our support team directly if you need further assistance.\n\nWe are committed to keeping your experience smooth and your device protected.
How do I block a sender?

To block someone, open their message and tap the block button at the top of the screen. Please note that this action instantly stops all new texts and alerts from that specific number.\n\nThis quick block stops annoying spam messages from showing up in your main inbox!

When you block a sender, Kuwago silently filters out all future messages from that number. You will no longer receive notifications or alerts from them.\n\nBlocked messages are still stored in the Blacklist tab so you can review them at any time.

No. Blocking is completely invisible to the sender. They will not be notified that their messages are being filtered.\n\nFrom their perspective, messages are sent normally — Kuwago simply prevents them from reaching your inbox.

1. Go to the Blacklist tab from the bottom navigation bar.
2. Find the sender you want to unblock.
3. Swipe left on their entry or tap the remove icon.
4. Confirm the unblock action when prompted.

Once unblocked, future messages from that sender will appear normally again.

Blocked messages are stored in the Blacklist tab. You can access it anytime from the bottom navigation bar to review all senders that have been blocked.\n\nThis allows you to keep track of who has been filtered without losing any history.

Yes! You can manually add a phone number or sender name to the blacklist.

1. Go to the Blacklist tab.
2. Tap the add button.
3. Enter the phone number or sender name.
4. Confirm to add it to your blocked list.

This is useful for preemptively blocking known spam numbers.
Why am I still getting alerts?
Why did the app stop running?

If you are still receiving alerts from a blocked sender, it may be because:

• The sender is using a different number.
• The block was applied to a sender name that has changed.
• The Notification Listener permission has been revoked.

Try re-checking your Blacklist entries and ensure Notification Access is enabled in Settings.

Android may stop Kuwago from running in the background to save battery. This is common on devices with aggressive battery optimization.

To fix this:
1. Go to your phone's Settings → Apps → Kuwago.
2. Tap Battery and select "Unrestricted" or "No restrictions."
3. Also ensure Notification Access remains enabled.

This allows Kuwago to continuously monitor incoming messages.

To ensure Kuwago can run properly in the background:

1. Open your phone's Settings.
2. Go to Apps → Kuwago → Battery.
3. Select "Unrestricted" or disable battery optimization.
4. Go back and check Notifications → ensure all are enabled.
5. Verify Notification Listener access is turned on under Special App Access.

These steps help prevent the system from killing the app while it protects you.

Share anonymized flagged messages to improve our detection models.

By enabling this, you allow anonymized versions of flagged messages to be securely shared with our team for use in retraining and improving the detection model.\n\nAll data is stripped of personal identifiers before submission. Your privacy is our priority.
Report harmful text messages to the authorities automatically

When enabled, messages confirmed as smishing or high-risk phishing will be automatically reported to the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) on your behalf.\n\nThis helps authorities take action against malicious senders and protects other users from the same threats.

This is optional, but it may help in quickly identifying malicious senders based on our stored list of blacklisted contacts.

The calling code of the Philippines is +63. To write a contact number in international format, simply replace the leading 0 with +63.

For example: a local mobile number like 0917-123-4567 becomes +63 917 123 4567 in the proper international format.

Likewise, we also support contact numbers from outside the Calling Code of the Philippines (other than +63).
Or enter sender name (e.g. GCash, BDO)
Changing the contents may affect its chance of being flagged as phishing.\n\nIf there are any links in the text message, kindly include them as well.
